data.name: Cosmo
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'kosmos', meaning order or harmony of the universe. In Christian tradition, it symbolizes the divine creation and the wisdom of the cosmos.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the divine order of the universe.
data.numerology_meaning: Those with the name Cosmo possess a unique perspective on life and a strong desire for freedom. They are adaptable, resourceful, and quick-thinking.

in_hebrew.name: קוסמו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מקור השם הוא יווני, ואף על פי שלא ישראלי, הוא יכול להיות שם יפה לילד יהודי-נוצרי, שכן 'קוסמו' מושך עליו אור הכוכבים, והוא תיאור יפה של יצירת האל. היו גם שם זה בשימוש בקהילות נוצריות, שם הלקוח מהיוונית, 'κοσμος', ומשמעותו 'עולם', 'יקום'.

in_greek.name: Κόσμο
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Κοσμος προέρχεται από τη λέξη κόσμος, που σημαίνει κόσμος, υφήλιο, είδος. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο Κόσμος αναφέρεται ως το σύνολο των πραγμάτων που υπάρχουν στο σύμπαν (Ιωάν. 1:10). Στη χριστιανική παράδοση, το όνομα Κοσμος συνδέεται με την κτίση και την ενέργεια του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Cosmo
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Cosmo derivatur a verbo graeco κόσμος, quod significat mundus, orbis terrarum. In Nova Testamento, mundus significat corpus humanum (I Ioan. 2:16). In traditione christiana, nomen Cosmo conecta se ad creaturam et energiam Dei.

in_english.name: Cosmo
in_english.long_meaning: The name Cosmo is derived from the Greek word κόσμος, meaning world, universe, or cosmos. In the New Testament, the world refers to the human body (1 John 2:16). In Christian tradition, the name Cosmo is associated with creation and the energy of God, reflecting a deep connection to the natural world and the divine. It is a fitting choice for a child who is seen as a gift from God, a tiny but vital part of the grand cosmic plan.

biblical_reference.note: Though not directly found in scripture, the concept of cosmos is deeply rooted in biblical themes of creation and the natural world.

saint_reference.note: There is no known patron saint with this name.

data.cultural_impact: In popular culture, the term 'Cosmo' has been used in various ways, from a magazine title (Cosmopolitan) to a comic book superhero (Cosmo the Space-Boy), reflecting the broad and diverse meanings associated with the cosmos, order, and harmony.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name 'Cosmo' as a given name can be seen as a reflection of one's belief in God as the Creator of the universe, representing the divine order and harmony in all things. It may also signify a person's deep appreciation for the beauty and wonder of God's creation, inspiring a sense of awe, reverence, and spiritual connection.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Cosmo was a Roman god of the sky and the universe. The name Cosmo carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

trends: popular as a name for boys
modern_usage.modern_context: Cosmo is a name that has seen a resurgence in popularity in recent times, particularly as a name for boys. It is often associated with the cosmos and the universe, and may be influenced by the historical use of the name as a Roman god of the sky.
